title: No register id in a comment, held by the lint

tasks.title: Held-file comments state their rule, not the register

Rewrite each comment or docstring in this task's files that cites a register id - P<n>, P<n>.<m>, P<n>.<m>-<suffix>, BF<n>, BUG-<n>, F<n>, U<n>.<m>, or a dg<n>/tk<n> label used as a citation, including bare 'since P<n>' asides - so it states the constraint of its block in plain words; what an id meant is in the private register (quality-gates-internal/PLAN.md and plans/), but no register text is copied. tasks.title: The citation lint reads parenthesised phase, task and bug ids
tasks.description: Extend _deps.register_citation_violations() so the rule the sweep applied is held. Today it reads fault ids everywhere and phase ids only in the paragraph-opening shape, and its markdown pass reads only those two. Add: a phase, task or bug id inside parentheses - (P12.3), (P79.8-5bh), (BUG-12), (since P56.6), (U3.1) - in a comment, a docstring or a scanned markdown file, and the same shapes in the markdown pass as in the .py pass. Leave alone, each pinned by an allow case: a noqa code list, an id glued to a word as a rendered-output example (audit-state(P1):), an id inside a backtick span carrying more than the id, a test's own case label, id-shape illustrations and fixture data, and the files CITATION_SCAN_EXEMPT already names. Measure the rule over the tree before and after and put the measurement's command in the function's docstring, with a WHAT IT CANNOT SEE paragraph naming the bare forms it deliberately does not read (a bare P<n> is indistinguishable from the pervasive legitimate id-shape prose). The live-tree case must read zero once P86.1-P86.3 have landed; if a hit remains, it is a citation the sweep missed and the fix is the comment, never the rule. tools/prove-gates.py must carry a red-first row for the new shape in both directions if its table requires one. No plan ids in comments; no numbers in prose.
